text:
Maria Chen: Heads-up: we're scheduling a short infra service refresh next Tue 2026-05-04 01:00-02:00 UTC for control-plane config rollout in us-east1. This will trigger rolling drains of a small subset of serving nodes (approx 10%) to apply kernel/driver fixes. Expected customer impact: brief request retries and mild latency spikes for affected shards. No data migrations. :calendar:
Lauren Wu: thanks — is that the low-traffic window we discussed? who is oncall for the handoff? :handshake:
Maria Chen: yes low-traffic window. @Lauren you're the handoff lead. I'll post the exact node list and drain script here shortly. Plan: 4 waves, 15m per wave drain + 5m validation. Total ~80m including buffer. We will update status.redwood.ai if we see >5% error rate.
Samir Patel: tech details: drain will use our saferoll script. sequence: 
```
# drain command (example)
./saferoll --region us-east1 --nodes node-ctrl-0,node-ctrl-1 --grace 120 --verify healthcheck
```
We'll have a fallback: if any wave shows > 2% 5xx or backend saturation we pause and revert config (toggle via `controlplane toggle-config rollback-2026-05-04`).
Devon Brooks: will support prepare customer comms. Draft below for customers impacted in the window (we'll only send to customers whose tokens route to us-east1):
"Dear customer, on Tue May 4 we will perform a short maintenance to improve stability. You may see occasional increased latency or transient errors for up to an hour. No action is required; we recommend retrying on 5xx. If you have strict SLAs please reply and we'll coordinate a dedicated slot"
Chris O'Neill: Quick Q: Dedicated customers pinned to VPC — will they be affected?
Samir Patel: Dedicated customers with pinned private pools won't be touched. This is control-plane nodes that coordinate autoscaling for hosted pools only. We'll exclude dedicated pools from the saferoll target list.
Lauren Wu: Oncall runbook for the night:
- 00:50 UTC: quick pre-check (health, disk, telemetry_green)
- 01:00: start wave 1 (nodes a,b)
- 01:15: validation (synthetic traffic + dashboards)
- 01:20: proceed to wave 2 or pause if >2% 5xx
- escalate to eng-sre if pause or rollback triggered
I will handoff to @Nina at 02:00 after final verification.
IncidentBot: [automated] Pager schedule updated: Lauren Wu -> Nina (02:00 UTC handoff). :robot_face:
Maria Chen: Status page draft (please review):
```
Status page: Scheduled maintenance (control-plane refresh)
Start: 2026-05-04 01:00 UTC
End: 2026-05-04 02:00 UTC (estimated)
Impact: Possible transient increased latency and retries for a subset of customers in us-east1. No data loss expected.
Action: No action required. We'll post updates during the window.
```
Devon Brooks: Customer email suggestion to developers (short):
"Heads up: short maintenance at 01:00 UTC May 4. Expect transient 5xx/latency for some requests. If you need absolute zero disruption, open a support ticket and we can coordinate"
Chris O'Neill: Can we add a line about SDK retries/backoffs? many customers rely on our guidance.
Maria Chen: good call. I'll add: "If possible, ensure client SDKs have exponential backoff (initial 200-500ms) and at least 3 retries."
Lauren Wu: Quick checklist for the ops channel during the window:
- link to node list + saferoll args
- grafana: controlplane-p95, request-5xx-rate, qps-by-shard
- synthetic job id `synth-maint-2026-05-04` running continuously
- slack thread pinned to #eng-oncall and ops runbook posted
Samir Patel: I'll create the saferoll job in CI and post the job id here before EOD. Also will seed a canary traffic set to validate route consistency.
Nina (scheduler): Acknowledged for handoff at 02:00 UTC — I'll take over final verification and post completion notice to status page.
Lauren Wu: any objections to sending a targeted heads-up to customers in us-east1 now? I can coordinate sending via support API. :email:
Devon Brooks: do it. I'll prepare the list and queue it for 00:30 UTC send.
Maria Chen: final note: if everything is green I'll post an "All clear" status update and a short postmortem template in #postmortems tomorrow. If we hit issues we'll follow incident playbook and communicate to customers immediately. Thanks all :thumbsup:
